correctness.rationale: The Alexander dual contains the entire (k-2)-skeleton and exactly one (k-1)-simplex for each connected k-vertex subset: if all k-deletions of k+1 vertices were connected, a short cycle would contradict girth. A connected k-subset is a tree; deleting an internal vertex supplies a private (k-2)-face, otherwise a second connector yields a cycle of length <=k+1. Private faces form a signed identity minor of boundary Φ: W_k→wedge^{k-1}U; hence Φ injective and primitively embedded, with free cokernel Q. Canonical augmentation contraction identifies skeleton cycles with wedge^{k-1}U, and signed integral equivariant Alexander duality plus UCT gives H_{N-k-1}=sgn_V ⊗ Q^vee, no other reduced homology. Independent exact mod-two simplicial boundary calculation for P8,k4 gave H3 dimension30=C(7,3)-5. The finite script is a check, not a proof.
residual_risks: The rational character alone cannot establish integral torsion-freeness, which here relies on the signed private-face unit minor.
